name: Zoho Cliq
verdict: Self-serve: register a Server-based client in the Zoho API Console, with no review documented, in about 1-3 days. Use the accounts domain that matches each customer's data center.
needGuide: Short one, plus a data-center check: register the client, add redirect URIs, route each customer to their own accounts domain.

auth.detail: Authorization-code flow against accounts.zoho.{dc}/oauth/v2/auth with response_type=code and access_type=offline; token at /oauth/v2/token. Access token lasts about 1 hour; refresh via grant_type=refresh_token; revoke at /oauth/v2/token/revoke. Header is Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken {token}. Each data center (.com, .eu, .in, .com.au and others) has its own accounts and API domain.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review); multi-data-center handling adds testing

approval.gate: None documented for the OAuth client itself. Marketplace/extension listing for Cliq is optional (not verified). Must use the accounts domain matching each customer's data center.

scopes.why: Per-endpoint scopes (ZohoCliq.<Resource>.<READ|CREATE|UPDATE|DELETE>); no scope-level review documented.
scopes.summary: Scopes per endpoint, format ZohoCliq.<Resource>.<READ|CREATE|UPDATE|DELETE>. No scope-level review is documented. Request only what the agent needs (channel read, message post).

cost: Free API; Cliq plan limits may apply to the customer's org (unverified)
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Zoho account owner on the developer side can register the client in the API Console; use a company-owned Zoho account, not a personal one.
Where you register: Zoho API Console → Add Client → Server-based Applications → enter client name, homepage/client domain, authorized redirect URIs → copy Client ID and Secret
Cost: Free API; Cliq plan limits may apply to the customer's org (unverified)

registerAt.path: Zoho API Console → Add Client → Server-based Applications → enter client name, homepage/client domain, authorized redirect URIs → copy Client ID and Secret

steps.do: Sign in to api-console.zoho.com (or the DC-specific console) with a company-owned Zoho account
Add Client → Server-based Applications; set redirect URI(s) and copy Client ID/Secret
List needed scopes (e.g. ZohoCliq.Channels.READ, messages scopes) and build the auth URL with access_type=offline&prompt=consent
Implement code exchange at {accounts-domain}/oauth/v2/token and store refresh tokens encrypted
Detect each customer's DC from the redirect/authorize response and route API calls to the matching domain
Implement refresh (1-hour access tokens) and revocation on disconnect
Run test calls against a Cliq org in two data centers

roles.team: Any Zoho account owner on the developer side can register the client in the API Console; use a company-owned Zoho account, not a personal one.
roles.console: none documented in the Cliq docs for API Console collaborators.
roles.customer: The authorizing user consents to scopes (e.g. ZohoCliq.Channels.READ). Some endpoints need extra scopes such as Zoho People. A Zoho org admin can likely restrict third-party app access; not verified.

testing: Create a free Zoho/Cliq org in the data center you target and run the full code flow.
Tokens are per DC, so test at least .com plus one other DC (.eu or .in).

blockers.problem: Wrong data-center domain gives invalid_client or redirect errors
blockers.fix: Store the customer's DC and use matching accounts and API domains.

blockers.problem: Doc says refresh tokens can be used a limited number of times (about 20 per the page)
Access token must be in the Authorization header, not the query string

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth flow, DC routing, refresh logic and Cliq API calls, draft scope justification and customer setup docs, run test calls once credentials exist.
automation.humanMust: Sign in to the Zoho API Console and create the client; customer user (or org admin) clicks consent.

uncertain: Whether a single client can serve multiple DCs (a Multi-DC option likely exists in the console) or needs one client per DC; marketplace listing requirements; org-admin controls for third-party apps; exact refresh-token limit wording.
